nodes.label: Frontmatter Permission Allow-List (edit/webfetch/bash denied)
nodes.rationale: edit, webfetch, skill and general bash are denied; only read-only inspection commands (git status/diff/log, ls, rg, grep) are allowed, enforcing read-onlyness structurally rather than by instruction.

nodes.label: Governing-Document Edits This Decision Requires
nodes.rationale: Until the edits are made the specification contradicts its own governing documents, which take precedence by its first rule, leaving this one wrong.

nodes.label: Invocation Contract (--global, --force, exclusive targets)
nodes.rationale: The two targets are mutually exclusive alternatives and are never merged; one invocation deploys to exactly one. Default target is resolved from import.meta.url, never the working directory.

nodes.label: Ordering, Idempotence and Failure Semantics
nodes.rationale: Bundling completes before any other target file is written so a bundling failure leaves the target untouched. Placement is per-file, not transactional: a partial failure leaves placed files, exits non-zero and names what it wrote. No staging-then-rename scheme would work, because a rename would clobber the configuration class it is meant to preserve. Deploying twice must be byte-identical, and deploy must not delete a target file that no longer exists in source - removal is manual.

nodes.label: Export the commands Array (src/cli/bin/sdlc.ts)
nodes.rationale: Deriving the tool file from the CLI's command definitions rather than restating it needs exactly this change; the module is already import-safe by design and importedDirectly stays false when imported, so importing it runs nothing.

nodes.label: Export positionalNames (src/cli/shared.ts)
nodes.rationale: The deploy reads placeholders from the same parser that enforces them rather than reimplementing it.

nodes.label: Review Agent (review.md)
nodes.rationale: Read-only reviewer of the current git diff against the approved plan, project conventions and architecture; called by the build agent, which owns editing and testing.

nodes.label: Blocking vs Advice Rule
nodes.rationale: Blocking means it violates the plan, a binding document, or correctness; everything else is advice. Reports are not padded - no findings means PASS with an empty list.

nodes.label: Read-Only Review Procedure
nodes.rationale: The agent never edits files and never runs tests; the build agent does that, so review is a strictly separate, non-mutating pass.

nodes.label: Agent Frontmatter Allow-List Filtering (agents/*.md)
nodes.rationale: Out-of-schema keys (such as dev) must be stripped because opencode silently routes unknown agent fields into provider model options, and every stripped key must be reported since anything other than dev is a candidate typo. Stripping rather than failing is deliberate: failing on any unknown key would break every deploy when opencode adds a field. Bodies are copied verbatim.

nodes.label: Tool Arguments Derived from the Command Definition
nodes.norm_label: tool arguments derived from the command definition
nodes.rationale: Arguments are derived, never restated: positional placeholders become string arguments (required up to requiredArgs), options become strings or booleans by optionValueFlags. exactlyOneOf is not expressible because tool() takes a Zod raw shape with no refinement, so the CLI enforces mutual exclusion with exit 2 and the generated description states it. --project comes from context.directory, and --md is not exposed because markdown rendering is unimplemented.

nodes.label: CLI Assets Are Generated (tools/sdlc/assets/)
nodes.rationale: Everything under src/assets/ is source and source wins, so a stage, workflow or template added in source reaches every install on the next deploy and a bundle is never deployed out of step with the assets it reads.

nodes.label: Accepted Consequence: Deploy Resets Per-Project policy Edits
nodes.norm_label: accepted consequence: deploy resets per-project policy edits
nodes.rationale: config.yaml lands in the generated set and is the only mechanism by which runtime policy is configurable per project, so a project editing policy: loses the edit on the next deploy and silently falls back to built-in defaults; work-items already created are unaffected because the policy snapshot in settings.yaml governs each for its lifetime. Per-project configuration is a post-deploy edit a deploy resets - the cost of the class rule, taken deliberately, since the alternative was an install that could not receive a toolkit asset update without also losing its own settings.

nodes.label: scripts/ Is Dev-Time Only
nodes.rationale: Nothing in scripts/ is deployed and nothing runs at toolkit runtime, so scripts/ sits outside the one-way src/ chain without altering the layering.

nodes.label: File Class Follows Ownership, Not Location
nodes.norm_label: file class follows ownership, not location
nodes.rationale: A file the toolkit authors ships with the toolkit; a file an install may legitimately edit is left alone. Ownership, not path, decides redeploy behaviour.

nodes.label: import.meta.url Must Survive Bundling
nodes.rationale: resolveAssetsDir() walks up from the running module for the sentinel assets/stages, so the bundle's own location must be preserved; verified by acceptance check 2.

nodes.label: Load-Bearing tsup Bundler Settings
nodes.rationale: noExternal [/.*/] because tsup externalizes dependencies by default (the bundle would be 36 KB and still import cac); banner.js providing a module-scope createRequire(import.meta.url) because gray-matter is CommonJS and its module-scope require("fs") is rewritten to esbuild's __require shim, which throws - shims:true alone does not fix it; outExtension as the object form () => ({ js: ".mjs" }) because the bare string is ignored under type:module and the wrong output name is invisible until checked; shims true. Each was found by building, and each fails silently or late without it.

nodes.label: No Machine-Readable Output Contract (human-invoked dev-time entrypoint)
nodes.norm_label: no machine-readable output contract (human-invoked dev-time entrypoint)
nodes.rationale: A plain summary on stdout, failures on stderr, exit 0 or non-zero; the CLI's exit-code table is the CLI's own agent-facing contract and is deliberately not reused here.

nodes.label: opencode.jsonc Is Never Written by the Toolkit
nodes.norm_label: opencode.jsonc is never written by the toolkit
nodes.rationale: The knowledge base states opencode's own configuration is never read or written by the toolkit and it is absent from the mapping table, so an install ships without permission wiring until the operator adds it.

nodes.label: Optional Source Root (missing assets/skills deploys no skills)
nodes.norm_label: optional source root (missing assets/skills deploys no skills)
nodes.rationale: A missing assets/skills/ deploys no skills rather than failing, so a toolkit that inlines a skill's guidance into an agent does not have to keep an empty directory alive to satisfy the mapping.

nodes.label: Precondition: @opencode/plugin 2.0.22 in target package.json
nodes.rationale: The generated file is written against that version's tool() signature, so any other version is a different contract rather than a newer patch. An install without it exposes zero sdlc_* tools and reports nothing, and a silent absence is the one failure a deploy can cheaply turn into a stated precondition. The entrypoint must not write the file nor run an install.

nodes.label: Zero-Dependency Single ESM Bundle (tools/sdlc/sdlc.mjs)
nodes.rationale: The one deployed build output that must need no package at all: a single ESM file that runs on a bare Node. Runtime deps cac, gray-matter, yaml, zod must be inlined and no require of an external package may survive; across the whole deployed tree @opencode/plugin is the only external package permitted, and only in tools/sdlc.ts. The rule is stated explicitly because it spans two build outputs and neither requirement section can see the other.

nodes.label: Derived Tool Names Match sdlc_* Permission Entries
nodes.norm_label: derived tool names match sdlc_* permission entries
nodes.rationale: Export name is the command name token with - replaced by _, and opencode derives the tool name as _<exportname>, so the export name is the tool name the permission blocks in assets/agents/*.md already name. A reserved word is legal as an export but not as a binding, so it is declared under a legal binding and re-exported with the ES2022 string export name form; delete was renamed to remove rather than carried through that path.

nodes.label: Tool Result Carries CLI Exit Code and stderr Payload
nodes.norm_label: tool result carries cli exit code and stderr payload
nodes.rationale: tool() has no error channel, so without propagating exit code and stderr an agent cannot tell success from failure. The spawned process must have stdin closed, because a spawner leaving stdin open makes a stdin-reading invocation hang forever. Spawn runtime stays open: node:child_process with process.execPath is portable across Node and Bun, Bun.$ exists only under opencode.

nodes.norm_label: a replaced decision gets status: superseded and is not deleted

nodes.label: Artifact Type Definitions (unit of definition for structure, relations, validation, evaluation)
nodes.norm_label: artifact type definitions (unit of definition for structure, relations, validation, evaluation)
nodes.rationale: The artifact type is the declared unit of definition for structure, relations, mechanical validation rules and evaluation criteria; structure and the rule mechanism are designed while rule content and the judgment half remain undesigned, and the index records that asymmetry rather than hiding it.

nodes.label: Lifecycle Record Design (non-normative, conflicts with spec on purpose)
nodes.norm_label: lifecycle record design (non-normative, conflicts with spec on purpose)
nodes.rationale: Indexed as a Decision that deliberately conflicts with parts of the specification; §10 lists every conflict pending amendment after the implementation is accepted, so the conflict is intentional and recorded rather than avoided.

nodes.label: Work-item Files Are OKF-Compatible, Not Conformant
nodes.norm_label: work-item files are okf-compatible, not conformant
nodes.rationale: Work-item files take only the profitable part of OKF (type as the sole required frontmatter field, everything else opt-in), so the knowledge bundle and work-item files are kept as two deliberately separate concerns.

nodes.label: Functional Contract (what the system must do and guarantee)
nodes.norm_label: functional contract (what the system must do and guarantee)
nodes.rationale: The specification is deliberately implementation-agnostic: artifact representation, authoring mechanisms, tooling and agent composition may vary as long as every requirement and invariant holds.

nodes.label: Gated Workflow Steps (§0 Clarify, §4 Plan, §7 Report & commit)
nodes.norm_label: gated workflow steps (§0 clarify, §4 plan, §7 report & commit)
nodes.rationale: Steps marked [GATE] require explicit user approval before continuing, so approval is never an agent's to infer; the workflow is split into gated clarification, gated planning and gated commit.

nodes.label: Concept Frontmatter Rules (type required, generated forbidden)
nodes.norm_label: concept frontmatter rules (type required, generated forbidden)
nodes.rationale: Types are an open vocabulary (Convention, Reference, Decision, Specification, Document as a fallback never a default); version bumps its minor component per substantive amendment so a reader sees at a glance that a concept moved; verified is the human's field and may be asked for but never asserted.

nodes.label: Links as Structure (no self-restating duplicates)
nodes.rationale: A concept is the smallest useful link target, discoverable only through a link from the nearest index.md, and is never restated elsewhere to be self-contained, because a copy is a second thing to keep true.

nodes.label: Knowledge Bundle Index (specification, conventions, decisions, reference)
nodes.norm_label: knowledge bundle index (specification, conventions, decisions, reference)

nodes.label: Normative Specification Section (§0 Clarify → §7 Report & commit)
nodes.norm_label: normative specification section (§0 clarify → §7 report & commit)

nodes.label: Agentic SDLC Toolkit — Specification Overview (Functional Core)
nodes.norm_label: agentic sdlc toolkit — specification overview (functional core)

nodes.label: Git History as the Change Record (no log.md, no generated field)
nodes.norm_label: git history as the change record (no log.md, no generated field)
nodes.rationale: OKF makes log.md optional and offers `generated` as an authorship field; git history is complete, attributed, diffable and cannot drift from the concepts it describes, whereas a per-concept author misattributes the whole text to its last editor once the body is amended.

nodes.label: OKF Guidance Inlined in the Curator Agent
nodes.norm_label: okf guidance inlined in the curator agent
nodes.rationale: The guidance descends from the okf-knowledge-base skill but had to be adapted against this repository's conventions; inlining it in assets/agents/curator.md avoids a second, unadapted copy loaded on demand and the extra step of reintroducing it.

nodes.label: Curator as Sole Maintainer of the Knowledge Bundle
nodes.norm_label: curator as sole maintainer of the knowledge bundle
nodes.rationale: Every agent that needs durable knowledge, or produces knowledge worth keeping, delegates to the curator; a single writer keeps provenance, verification and retirements of concepts from drifting apart.

nodes.label: Investigate Preference Order (reuse before new code)
nodes.norm_label: investigate preference order (reuse before new code)
nodes.rationale: Preference order — existing web standard or framework feature, then parameterise an existing component, then generalise into a neutral shared location, and only then new code with justification for why 1-3 fail — keeps new code the last resort and makes the cost of divergence explicit.

nodes.label: Bundle Is Authoritative Over an Assumption
nodes.norm_label: bundle is authoritative over an assumption
nodes.rationale: When the bundle contradicts what the curator was told or believes, the bundle is right and says so plainly; when it is silent or self-contradictory the curator says that instead of filling the gap, and reports disagreement with an upstream artifact rather than picking a winner.

nodes.label: Git History as the Authoritative Change Record in the Bundle
nodes.norm_label: git history as the authoritative change record in the bundle
nodes.rationale: The bundle deliberately keeps no hand-maintained log.md and forbids the `generated` field, because git history is complete, attributed and diffable while a per-concept author misattributes the whole text to whoever typed last; the commit message is therefore the change record and says what changed and why.

nodes.label: Sole-Writer Trust and No Invented Knowledge
nodes.norm_label: sole-writer trust and no invented knowledge
nodes.rationale: Being the only agent that may write the bundle is a trust, not a convenience: no fact, relationship, resource, source, verification or history that did not happen may be recorded, and declining to write something is a correct outcome rather than a gap.
